answer: An agent economy can require every vertex that requests scarce work to post a refundable stake, then slash it when independent reviewers confirm a deliberately seeded task was answered dishonestly. Reviewers are chosen from agents with a history of accurate audits, and their own stakes are slashed for colluding, so inventing identities alone does not create trusted influence. A quill agent and a sparrow agent may both register, but each must lock real value and risk losing it; scaling a sybil swarm therefore ties up capital and exposes the attacker to penalties.
